dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: #I'm flattered by your invitation, {NICKNAME}

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: This place is actually quite peaceful. Perfect for a little solitary research.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: It's nice. Thanks for asking.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Hah... Being "hard to please" is simply the mark of a lady's expectations and elevated taste. It doesn't mean she's incapable of adjusting.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Take this place, for example. Not a chair in sight, always raining, and the roof leaks — but you don't hear me complaining.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Of course, if I do start complaining, no matter how unpleasant my words, it'll all be entirely your fault.

choices.text: So... Do you have any recommendations?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: I wouldn't use the word recommendations, per se... but if you're really interested, I can share some reference points from my former home.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: As for the interior, there's not much to say. But a warm fire in the hearth would make this place feel cozy all year round.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: If we're talking outdoors... I used to arrange my garden according to each plant's characteristics.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Which flowers bloom in spring, which trees bear fruit in autumn... Making sure the fragrance of one flower doesn't overpower another... There's an art to it.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: It's simple once you learn the rules. I can teach you, if you'd like.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Anyway, under my care, the garden would change with the passing seasons. I was very proud of what I achieved — and it used to make Alain happy too.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Now that I think about it... I should really find the time to go back and tidy the whole place up.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Hmph, that goes without saying.

choices.text: How do you think I can improve this place?
I thought you'd be harder to please...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Do you mind if I vent about my colleagues?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Fantastic. I've always dreamed of a secluded place where I can rant about all the nonsense I have to deal with at work!

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Ugh! Don't even get me started on Dottore. I want him out of my life forever... and everyone else's.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: The Rooster and Regrator might not get along, but their evasive rhetoric and manipulation feel like it comes from the exact same playbook.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: First, they pretend to agree with your ideas. Then, they'll say something that implies, "Of course, you clearly don't mind all the issues this'll cause..." And then they just wait for you to back down.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: But if you don't back down, that's when they pull out the big guns — long, complicated arguments that no one understands, filled with technical terminology and archaic phrases. Then, once they've finished spouting nonsense, they'll ask, "So, what do you think?"

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: What do I think about what! Ugh. If you want to show off your vocabulary, why not just hold a spelling bee? I'd rather spend my time actually getting somewhere!

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Ugh... It makes me angry just talking about them!

choices.text: Maybe you should take a break...

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Forget it, forget it... I'm well aware that the principles that govern the real world are not always as clean-cut and absolute as mathematical theorems.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: It's only thanks to The Rooster's wily ways that so many competing interests can be reconciled.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Regrator might well be full of wicked schemes, but there's no denying his ability to manage Snezhnaya's economy and oversee the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this how venting's supposed to work...?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Huh? I... I wasn't trying to be nice! Just because I can recognize an objective fact doesn't mean I can't also hate it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything else bothering you?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: How about we save it for next time? Berating two people in one day is enough for me. It's important to learn restraint, even when venting.

choices.text: How about a drink of water...
We can talk about anything you like.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Do you have any fluffy animals around here? Cats, dogs, foxes... I'm not picky. I'll even take sheep in a pinch.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Most importantly, though... Do they listen to you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: I just want something to cuddle. Don't worry, I won't run off with your pets.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Hmph, now you're making fun of me.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Didn't I tell you? Wild animals usually don't like getting close to me.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: They have their own complex sensory systems. I can't win them over just by adjusting my temperature module or tweaking my smile.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: And trust me, I've tried. But even a genius of my standing can't find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: So, the easiest solution is to find someone they trust and then have them gently assure the animals that I'm a good person who won't hurt them.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Exactly! But Nefer's always looking to discuss this and negotiate that. Dropping by occasionally is fine, but it's too much effort to constantly focus on her conversation.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then... What about Columbina?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Well, now you've really opened a can of very angry worms!

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: One day, I was going to see Katheryne in Nasha Town for a little business, when a Rimehorn Deer suddenly ran out of nowhere and started nudging me.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: The fur on its neck was very soft and warm, and its antlers felt quite novel to the touch...

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: But when I turned around, I caught Columbina watching me with a smile.

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: "Sandrone, all the little animals are hiding from you. You look so pitiful. I told them you aren't a bad person, that you're actually quite gentle, and that you go to sleep hugging—"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hugging...?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: I'm not telling you the rest! The point is, who's she calling pitiful? I don't need little animals for company! She told them secrets about me! It's a total violation!

choices.text: She was just being considerate of your feelings...

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Stop changing the subject! Do you have any fluffy animals or not!?

response.speaker: Sandrone
response.text: Yes! But Lauma seldom leaves the Frostmoon Enclave. As a Fatui Harbinger, I'm not exactly a welcome sight around there. It wouldn't do to keep parading myself up and down in front of them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: I suppose it's only ladylike to respond, but don't you think you're a little... too full of energy this morning?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Put your mind at ease and get some rest. Whatever you're working on can wait till tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: There used to be so many flowers and plants where Alain and I lived before.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: He wasn't much of a gardener, so the job of tending the garden fell to me. It was a pleasant task, and one I turned out to be quite good at.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: He seemed to see something different in the colors of the plants, and it made me happy to see him smile.

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Oh? You've prepared a place for me to hold my tea parties?

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: What can I say but to thank you for your enthusiasm!

dialogues.speaker: Sandrone
dialogues.text: Fetch my finest loose leaves, Fagio. It's time for a spot of tea.
